meta.title: oh-my-workflow — parallel repo checks through coding-agent CLIs
meta.desc: Run independent coding-agent repo checks in parallel, assemble one result from shape-validated node outputs, and journal failures.

landing.pill: parallel repo checks, one shaped result
landing.tagline: Run independent checks through claude -p or codex exec, assemble one result from shape-validated node outputs, and journal every node attempt.
landing.twinSub: The vocabulary resembles host-native workflow tools; omw runs whole external CLI processes and does not claim host-level parity.
landing.twinNativeLabel: native dynamic Workflow — inside Claude Code
landing.diffLegend: <mark class="ins">marked</mark> = the only two spots that change.
landing.honestTitle: This is slower and pricier than a raw-API orchestrator — on purpose.
landing.honestBody: A node is a whole coding agent, not one completion: it reads your repo, runs tools, and iterates. You pay process and agent-loop overhead per node. JSON Schema validates shape, not truth, and the journal is a runtime receipt rather than source provenance.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.intro: oh-my-workflow (omw) runs whole coding-agent CLIs as nodes in a plain-JS workflow. It is built for independent repo checks that run in parallel and assemble one result from shape-validated node outputs while journaling failures.
docs.quickstartBody: The built-in fake adapter needs no API key or agent network call; cloning and installing still use the network:
docs.hookAgentBody: Run one coding-agent CLI node. With a schema, omw validates and re-prompts the node with the errors up to 2×. Never throws (the null-contract) — except budget exhaustion.
docs.hookFlowBody: Per-item flow vs. barrier. Default to pipeline.
docs.adaptersBody: A node is a coding agent driven through its headless prompt→result CLI: fake, claude, codex, hermes, pi (planned). A missing CLI exits 3 with an install hint.
